summary: Prorated refund line appears as negative finalized invoice after private-fallback with quantized variant
description:
Issue summary:
Customer BrightHealth AI reports a negative (refund) line on their finalized monthly invoice for 2026-03 that they did not request. The line item is labeled as a prorated refund for a 'quantized-variant-rate' and corresponds to a ~$4,200 negative charge. Customer asserts their reserved dedicated capacity and private deployment should have absorbed any fallback usage and that no manual refund was requested.

Impact:
- Customer sees a negative invoice line causing accounting confusion and potentially delayed payment processing by their finance team.
- Customer is enterprise tier and needs a justified ledger entry and corrected invoice explanation for their auditors.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) with private connector to our postback endpoint. Primary region eu-west, fallback to hosted in us-west during brief VPN outage.

Observed:
- Finalized invoice includes a refund line: "PRORATE_REFUND: quantized-variant-rate" amount -$4,197.50.
- Billing ledger shows a corresponding debit adjustment but no support ticket or manual refund action recorded.
- Postback logs show doubled postbacks from the private connector around 2026-03-09T02:17Z during the connector VPN flapping window.

Expected:
- No prorated refund should appear unless support or billing automation performed a refund. Fallback usage should have been billed at the expected blended tariff and, if necessary, a reserve-buffer adjustment applied (not a refund).
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer runs mixed workload using open-llama-13b-quantized pinned to reserved capacity on private deployment.
2) At 2026-03-09T02:15Z, their private connector experienced a brief VPN interruption and retransmission window.
3) Client retried requests locally which led to duplicated postback delivery to billing reconciler during reconnection.
4) Billing reconciler deduplicator failed to detect collision due to a fingerprinting change when quantized variant metadata was present.
5) Final invoice run on 2026-03-10 incorporated reconciler adjustments and produced a prorated refund line.
logs:
Sample events from postback stream (redacted):
- 2026-03-09T02:16:58Z POST /postback v=1 fingerprint=abc123 variant=quantized meta:{warmup:true} status=200
- 2026-03-09T02:17:03Z POST /postback v=1 fingerprint=abc123 variant=quantized meta:{warmup:true, retry=1} status=200
- Reconciler: dedupe check fingerprint mismatch (found similar fingerprint with different metadata) -> treated as distinct events -> adjustment applied.
- Billing ledger entry ID BL-99877 created 2026-03-10T05:23Z: type=credit_adjustment amount=4197.50 reason="prorate-refund-quantized-variant"
investigation_notes: Support triage: confirmed invoice line exists and matches customer's reported amount.
Billing team: reproduced ledger adjustment entry and linked it to reconciler job run job_id=rc-2026-03-10-05.
SRE: private connector logs show VPN flapping between 02:15-02:20Z with ~18 retransmissions from customer side.

Reconciler hypothesis: dedupe algorithm uses (fingerprint, metadata_hash). Quantized variant added metadata that mutated metadata_hash on retry, causing duplicate recognition as separate usage and triggering a postback correction path that created a prorated refund instead of a reserve reclassification.
Early mitigation: Disabled automatic prorate-refund rule for reconciler run id=rc-2026-03-10-05 pending patch.
Repo note: a patch to normalize metadata before dedupe is in review at PR #478 (see linked PR).
comments: Priya Nair (Support) 2026-03-10: Acknowledge receipt. Opening task with billing and SRE. Advising customer we're investigating and will pause automated ledger corrections.
Customer (BrightHealth AI) 2026-03-10: We need a formal explanation for our auditors and to know if this will show up as a pending credit against next cycle. Please escalate.

Liam O'Connor (Billing) 2026-03-11: Confirmed reconciler created BL-99877. Temporarily disabled prorate-refund automation for reconciler runs touching private-fallback events. Working on fix to normalize metadata hashing.

SRE (Marcus Lee) 2026-03-11: VPN provider reported a brief certificate rotation at ~02:16Z which caused connector re-establishment behavior. We'll stabilise private connector and add additional jitter on retry to avoid duplicate postback bursts.

Liam O'Connor 2026-03-12: Proposed remediation: 1) Reverse BL-99877 with manual ledger entry and create a corrective invoice note. 2) Deploy reconciler patch to normalize metadata before fingerprinting (PR #478). 3) Re-run reconciler for affected window to regenerate correct adjustments.
workarounds:
- Immediate manual ledger reversal scheduled: create opposite adjustment and attach memo referencing SUP-739101.
- Provide customer with an interim credit memo PDF for auditors until corrected invoice is issued.
resolution: In progress: manual reversal planned and reconciler patch under review. No final resolution yet; target to complete ledger correction and issue corrected invoice by 2026-03-15.
